{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Fy4bysTfzwrF9hRg37kZVV","type":"tool_result","content":"# ERC-8004: Trustless Agents - Key Interfaces\n\n## 1. IdentityRegistry Interface\n\n**Core Registration Functions:**\n```solidity\nfunction register(string agentURI, MetadataEntry[] calldata metadata) \n  external returns (uint256 agentId)\n\nfunction register(string agentURI) external returns (uint256 agentId)\n\nfunction register() external returns (uint256 agentId)\n```\n\n**Metadata Management:**\n```solidity\nfunction getMetadata(uint256 agentId, string memory metadataKey) \n  external view returns (bytes memory)\n\nfunction setMetadata(uint256 agentId, string memory metadataKey, \n  bytes memory metadataValue) external\n```\n\n**Agent Wallet Functions:**\n```solidity\nfunction setAgentWallet(uint256 agentId, address newWallet, \n  uint256 deadline, bytes calldata signature) external\n\nfunction getAgentWallet(uint256 agentId) external view returns (address)\n\nfunction unsetAgentWallet(uint256 agentId) external\n```\n\n**URI Management:**\n```solidity\nfunction setAgentURI(uint256 agentId, string calldata newURI) external\n```\n\n**Key Events:**\n- `event Registered(uint256 indexed agentId, string agentURI, address indexed owner)`\n- `event MetadataSet(uint256 indexed agentId, string indexed indexedMetadataKey, string metadataKey, bytes metadataValue)`\n- `event URIUpdated(uint256 indexed agentId, string newURI, address indexed updatedBy)`\n\n---\n\n## 2. ReputationRegistry Interface\n\n**Feedback Submission:**\n```solidity\nfunction giveFeedback(uint256 agentId, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, \n  string calldata tag1, string calldata tag2, string calldata endpoint, \n  string calldata feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash) external\n```\n\n**Feedback Management:**\n```solidity\nfunction revokeFeedback(uint256 agentId, uint64 feedbackIndex) external\n\nfunction appendResponse(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress, \n  uint64 feedbackIndex, string calldata responseURI, \n  bytes32 responseHash) external\n```\n\n**Read Functions:**\n```solidity\nfunction readFeedback(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress, \n  uint64 feedbackIndex) external view returns (int128 value, \n  uint8 valueDecimals, string tag1, string tag2, bool isRevoked)\n\nfunction readAllFeedback(uint256 agentId, address[] calldata clientAddresses, \n  string tag1, string tag2, bool includeRevoked) external view returns \n  (address[] memory clients, uint64[] memory feedbackIndexes, \n  int128[] memory values, uint8[] memory valueDecimals, \n  string[] memory tag1s, string[] memory tag2s, bool[] memory revokedStatuses)\n\nfunction getSummary(uint256 agentId, address[] calldata clientAddresses, \n  string tag1, string tag2) external view returns (uint64 count, \n  int128 summaryValue, uint8 summaryValueDecimals)\n\nfunction getClients(uint256 agentId) external view returns (address[] memory)\n\nfunction getLastIndex(uint256 agentId, address clientAddress) \n  external view returns (uint64)\n```\n\n**Key Events:**\n- `event NewFeedback(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex, int128 value, uint8 valueDecimals, string indexed indexedTag1, string tag1, string tag2, string endpoint, string feedbackURI, bytes32 feedbackHash)`\n- `event FeedbackRevoked(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 indexed feedbackIndex)`\n- `event ResponseAppended(uint256 indexed agentId, address indexed clientAddress, uint64 feedbackIndex, address indexed responder, string responseURI, bytes32 responseHash)`\n\n---\n\n## 3. Agent Registration File Structure\n\n**Required Location & Format:**\n\nThe agent registration file resolves via the agent's URI (IPFS, HTTPS, or base64 data URI). For HTTPS endpoints, optional domain verification requires publishing to: `\"https://{endpoint-domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json\"`\n\n**Mandatory Top-Level Fields:**\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1\",\n  \"name\": \"agentName\",\n  \"description\": \"Natural language description\",\n  \"image\": \"https://example.com/image.png\"\n}\n```\n\n**Required Nested Structure - Registrations Array:**\n```json\n{\n  \"registrations\": [\n    {\n      \"agentId\": 22,\n      \"agentRegistry\": \"{namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry}\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Optional Trust Model Declaration:**\n```json\n{\n  \"supportedTrust\": [\"reputation\", \"crypto-economic\", \"tee-attestation\"]\n}\n```\n\n**Services Array** allows flexible endpoints (A2A, MCP, ENS, DID, email, etc.) with `name`, `endpoint`, and optional `version` fields."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"8f756a31-55a9-4936-b422-86b6df483d93","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:27:51.904Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":74013,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# ERC-8004: Trustless Agents - Key Interfaces\n\n## 1. A client hits your URL → you reply 402 Payment Required with a JSON Payment Requirements object → the client pays and retries with an X-PAYMENT header → you verify/settle → respond 200 OK.\n\n## Payment Flow and Headers\n\nThe resource server responds with a 402 Payment Required status and a PaymentRequired b64 object return as a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. Client selects one of the PaymentRequirements returned by the server response and creates a PaymentPayload based on the scheme & network of the PaymentRequirements they have selected.\n\nClient sends the HTTP request with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header containing the PaymentPayload to the resource server. Resource server returns a 200 OK response to the Client with the resource they requested as the body of the HTTP response, and a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header containing the Settlement Response as Base64 encoded JSON if the payment was executed successfully.\n\n## Schemes and Exact Payment Scheme\n\nA scheme is a logical way of moving money. The x402 protocol is extensible to different ways of settling payments via its scheme field. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QqvAvkDGhBDPzVRhdRUvnf","type":"tool_result","content":"# ERC-8004 ReputationRegistry Analysis\n\n## (a) Who Can Call giveFeedback and Sybil/Auth Handling\n\n**Eligibility:** \"The feedback submitter MUST NOT be the agent owner or an approved operator for agentId.\"\n\nAnyone else can call `giveFeedback()`. The spec explicitly states: \"New feedback can be added by any clientAddress calling:\" the function.\n\n**Sybil/Spam Mitigation:** The protocol acknowledges the vulnerability: \"Sybil attacks are possible, inflating the reputation of fake agents.\" However, rather than implementing on-chain proof-of-payment or FeedbackAuth mechanisms, it delegates this to external reputation systems built around reviewers: \"we expect many players to build reputation systems, for example, trusting or giving reputation to reviewers.\"\n\nThe `endpoint` parameter is described as \"a file URI pointing to an off-chain JSON containing additional information\" and represents \"the Endpoint reachable\" or associated service endpoint being reviewed.\n\n**No FeedbackAuth or x402 enforcement on-chain** for giveFeedback itself.\n\n## (b) Exact Off-Chain Feedback File Fields\n\nWhen a feedbackURI is provided, the optional file structure includes:\n\n**Required fields:**\n- agentRegistry, agentId, clientAddress, createdAt, value, valueDecimals\n\n**Optional fields:**\n- tag1, tag2, endpoint, mcp (with tool/prompt/resource), a2a (with skills, contextId, taskId), oasf (with skills, domains), proofOfPayment (fromAddress, toAddress, chainId, txHash), and \"other fields [MAY]\"\n\n## (c) x402 and Payments Mentions\n\nYes, the spec mentions x402 twice:\n\n1. \"Payments are orthogonal to this protocol...However, examples are provided showing how x402 payments can enrich feedback signals.\"\n\n2. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QCuxpgfwERnFANP4N4QYWT","type":"tool_result","content":"# X402 Protocol v2 Technical Reference\n\n## HTTP Headers and Version Info\n\nThe specification document does **not** explicitly define HTTP header names for the 402 response or client payment submission. The document states it is \"transport-agnostic,\" meaning implementation details depend on the specific transport specification (e.g., HTTP transport spec), which is not included in this v2 specification.\n\n**Protocol version:** `\"x402Version\": 2` (numeric field in JSON payloads)\n\nThe document notes: \"This specification is based on the x402 protocol implementation\" but explicitly states transport-specific details are \"out of scope\" from the core v2 spec.\n\n## Core Data Structures\n\n**PaymentRequired** contains: `x402Version`, `error` (optional), `resource` object, `accepts` array, and `extensions` object.\n\n**PaymentRequirements** (within `accepts`): `scheme`, `network`, `amount`, `asset`, `payTo`, `maxTimeoutSeconds`, and `extra` (optional).\n\n**PaymentPayload** structure for \"exact\" EVM scheme:\n```json\n{\n  \"x402Version\": 2,\n  \"resource\": {...},\n  \"accepted\": {...},\n  \"payload\": {\n    \"signature\": \"0x...\",\n    \"authorization\": {\n      \"from\", \"to\", \"value\", \"validAfter\", \"validBefore\", \"nonce\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"extensions\": {}\n}\n```\n\n## Facilitator APIs\n\n**POST /verify** and **POST /settle** both accept: `x402Version`, `paymentPayload`, `paymentRequirements`\n\n**Settlement response** includes: `success` (boolean), `payer`, `transaction`, `network`, `amount` (optional), `extensions` (optional), and `errorReason` (if failed).\n\nThe specification does **not** detail settlement response HTTP headers, as those fall under transport-specific documentation."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"5f44ddd4-c214-42cb-aae9-5171bebbc7b3","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:28:23.973Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":465441,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# X402 Protocol v2 Technical Reference\n\n## HTTP Headers and Version Info\n\nThe specification document does **not** explicitly define HTTP header names for the 402 response or client payment submission. The document states it is \"transport-agnostic,\" meaning implementation details depend on the specific transport specification (e.g., HTTP transport spec), which is not included in this v2 specification.\n\n**Protocol version:** `\"x402Version\": 2` (numeric field in JSON payloads)\n\nThe document notes: \"This specification is based on the x402 protocol implementation\" but explicitly states transport-specific details are \"out of scope\" from the core v2 spec.\n\n## Core Data Structures\n\n**PaymentRequired** contains: `x402Version`, `error` (optional), `resource` object, `accepts` array, and `extensions` object.\n\n**PaymentRequirements** (within `accepts`): `scheme`, `network`, `amount`, `asset`, `payTo`, `maxTimeoutSeconds`, and `extra` (optional).\n\n**PaymentPayload** structure for \"exact\" EVM scheme:\n```json\n{\n  \"x402Version\": 2,\n  \"resource\": {...},\n  \"accepted\": {...},\n  \"payload\": {\n    \"signature\": \"0x...\",\n    \"authorization\": {\n      \"from\", \"to\", \"value\", \"validAfter\", \"validBefore\", \"nonce\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"extensions\": {}\n}\n```\n\n## Facilitator APIs\n\n**POST /verify** and **POST /settle** both accept: `x402Version`, `paymentPayload`, `paymentRequirements`\n\n**Settlement response** includes: `success` (boolean), `payer`, `transaction`, `network`, `amount` (optional), `extensions` (optional), and `errorReason` (if failed).\n\nThe specification does **not** detail settlement response HTTP headers, as those fall under transport-specific documentation.","durationMs":7037,"url":"https://github.com/coinbase/x402/blob/main/specs/x402-specification-v2.md"}}

The \"exact\" scheme uses EIP-3009 (Transfer with Authorization) to enable secure, gasless transfers of specific amounts of ERC-20 tokens.\n\n## EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization\n\nEIP-3009 is an Ethereum standard that adds a transferWithAuthorization function to ERC-20 tokens, allowing gasless transfers where the token holder signs an off-chain authorization and a third party submits the transaction.\n\n## Payload Structure\n\nThe payload for EVM chains using the \"exact\" scheme contains authorization objects that follow EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization, with fields including: from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, and nonce. Additionally, the extra field in payment acceptance details includes name and version information (e.g., \"name\": \"USD Coin\", \"version\": \"2\").\n\n## Base, USDC, and CDP/Facilitator\n\nBase is identified by the CAIP-2 namespace eip155:8453, and is the default in most x402 docs because Coinbase is the issuer of the chain and the protocol's incubator. CDP stands for Coinbase Developer Platform, the infrastructure arm of Coinbase that provides the primary x402 facilitator, SDKs, and developer documentation.\n\nThe search results also reference the Coinbase GitHub repository at `https://github.com/coinbase/x402` which contains the complete x402 specification and implementation details.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"331c0684-6e75-4699-afde-3858ae3d284f","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:28:25.842Z","tool_use_result":{"query":"x402 \"exact\" scheme EVM EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization payload extra name version USDC Base facilitator CDP url","results":[{"tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_01THMYgRmnaUmPZBB6YbrrEd","content":[{"title":"evm package - The \"exact\" scheme uses EIP-3009 (Transfer with Authorization) to enable secure, gasless transfers of specific amounts of ERC-20 tokens.\n\n## EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization\n\nEIP-3009 is an Ethereum standard that adds a transferWithAuthorization function to ERC-20 tokens, allowing gasless transfers where the token holder signs an off-chain authorization and a third party submits the transaction.\n\n## Payload Structure\n\nThe payload for EVM chains using the \"exact\" scheme contains authorization objects that follow EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization, with fields including: from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, and nonce. Additionally, the extra field in payment acceptance details includes name and version information (e.g., \"name\": \"USD Coin\", \"version\": \"2\").\n\n## Base, USDC, and CDP/Facilitator\n\nBase is identified by the CAIP-2 namespace eip155:8453, and is the default in most x402 docs because Coinbase is the issuer of the chain and the protocol's incubator. CDP stands for Coinbase Developer Platform, the infrastructure arm of Coinbase that provides the primary x402 facilitator, SDKs, and developer documentation.\n\nThe search results also reference the Coinbase GitHub repository at `https://github.com/coinbase/x402` which contains the complete x402 specification and implementation details."],"durationSeconds":8.103131569999999,"searchCount":1}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FvoCe84xSey5S8sA4HRUcy","type":"tool_result","content":"# X402 Exact Scheme on EVM: Key Details\n\n## Asset Transfer Methods\n\nThe specification supports three approaches depending on token capabilities:\n\n1. **EIP-3009**: For tokens with native `transferWithAuthorization` (e.g., USDC)\n2. **Permit2**: Universal fallback using a proxy contract for any ERC-20\n3. **ERC-7710**: Smart accounts with delegation support\n\n## Payment Payload Structure (Permit2 Example)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"x402Version\": 2,\n  \"accepted\": {\n    \"scheme\": \"exact\",\n    \"network\": \"eip155:84532\",\n    \"amount\": \"10000\",\n    \"payTo\": \"0x209693Bc6afc0C5328bA36FaF03C514EF312287C\",\n    \"maxTimeoutSeconds\": 60,\n    \"asset\": \"0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e\",\n    \"extra\": {\n      \"assetTransferMethod\": \"permit2\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"payload\": {\n    \"signature\": \"0x2d6a7588...\",\n    \"permit2Authorization\": {\n      \"permitted\": {\"token\": \"0x036CbD5...\", \"amount\": \"10000\"},\n      \"from\": \"0x857b0651...\",\n      \"spender\": \"0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001\",\n      \"deadline\": \"1740672154\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Verification Steps\n\n**Permit2 verification requires:**\n- \"Verify payload.signature is valid and recovers to the permit2Authorization.from\"\n- Check client Permit2 allowance status\n- Confirm sufficient asset balance\n- Validate deadline and timing windows\n- Simulate the proxy settlement call\n\n## Settlement\n\n**Standard Permit2**: Call `x402ExactPermit2Proxy.settle`\n\n**With EIP-2612 Permit**: Call `x402ExactPermit2Proxy.settleWithPermit`\n\n**ERC-7710**: Call `delegationManager.redeemDelegations()` with delegation proof and execution calldata\n\n## Key Header Names\n\n- `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`: Contains signature and authorization parameters\n\nThe facilitator broadcasts transactions but cannot modify amounts or destinations—the client controls fund flow cryptographically."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"053682dd-0e74-4f08-a732-c65ac6579134","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:28:39.142Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":19006,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# X402 Exact Scheme on EVM: Key Details\n\n## Asset Transfer Methods\n\nThe specification supports three approaches depending on token capabilities:\n\n1. **EIP-3009**: For tokens with native `transferWithAuthorization` (e.g., USDC)\n2. **Permit2**: Universal fallback using a proxy contract for any ERC-20\n3. **ERC-7710**: Smart accounts with delegation support\n\n## Payment Payload Structure (Permit2 Example)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"x402Version\": 2,\n  \"accepted\": {\n    \"scheme\": \"exact\",\n    \"network\": \"eip155:84532\",\n    \"amount\": \"10000\",\n    \"payTo\": \"0x209693Bc6afc0C5328bA36FaF03C514EF312287C\",\n    \"maxTimeoutSeconds\": 60,\n    \"asset\": \"0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e\",\n    \"extra\": {\n      \"assetTransferMethod\": \"permit2\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"payload\": {\n    \"signature\": \"0x2d6a7588...\",\n    \"permit2Authorization\": {\n      \"permitted\": {\"token\": \"0x036CbD5...\", \"amount\": \"10000\"},\n      \"from\": \"0x857b0651...\",\n      \"spender\": \"0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001\",\n      \"deadline\": \"1740672154\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Verification Steps\n\n**Permit2 verification requires:**\n- \"Verify payload.signature is valid and recovers to the permit2Authorization.from\"\n- Check client Permit2 allowance status\n- Confirm sufficient asset balance\n- Validate deadline and timing windows\n- Simulate the proxy settlement call\n\n## Settlement\n\n**Standard Permit2**: Call `x402ExactPermit2Proxy.settle`\n\n**With EIP-2612 Permit**: Call `x402ExactPermit2Proxy.settleWithPermit`\n\n**ERC-7710**: Call `delegationManager.redeemDelegations()` with delegation proof and execution calldata\n\n## Key Header Names\n\n- `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`: Contains signature and authorization parameters\n\nThe facilitator broadcasts transactions but cannot modify amounts or destinations—the client controls fund flow cryptographically.","durationMs":9544,"url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coinbase/x402/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md"}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01VAt9iNhkDbmYdxFaonLqVR","type":"tool_result","content":"# x402 HTTP 402 Payment Flow\n\nBased on the documentation provided, here's the payment flow framework:\n\n## Header Names\n\nThe protocol uses three standardized headers:\n\n1. **Challenge**: `\"PAYMENT-REQUIRED\"` - server to client with payment details\n2. **Payment**: `\"PAYMENT-SIGNATURE\"` - client to server with authorization\n3. **Response**: `\"PAYMENT-RESPONSE\"` - server to client with settlement outcome\n\n## Encoding\n\n`\"All headers contain valid Base64-encoded JSON strings. This encoding ensures compatibility across different HTTP implementations and prevents issues with special characters in JSON payloads.\"`\n\n## Key Limitation\n\nThe documentation does not include:\n- Specific example JSON bodies with all fields\n- Sample client request headers\n- Sample settlement response headers\n- The x402Version field specification\n\n## What's Documented\n\nThe headers communicate:\n- Payment requirements (amount, currency, destination)\n- Client authorization proof\n- Settlement success/failure feedback\n\nThe flow supports both immediate settlement (`exact`, `upto` schemes) and deferred onchain redemption (`batch-settlement`), depending on the selected scheme.\n\nTo access complete examples and version details, the documentation suggests consulting the full index at https://docs.x402.org/llms.txt."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"6c7e5e8f-5d32-4d4f-b464-03e6ef2ca217","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:28:56.903Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":3400,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# x402 HTTP 402 Payment Flow\n\nBased on the documentation provided, here's the payment flow framework:\n\n## Header Names\n\nThe protocol uses three standardized headers:\n\n1. **Challenge**: `\"PAYMENT-REQUIRED\"` - server to client with payment details\n2. **Payment**: `\"PAYMENT-SIGNATURE\"` - client to server with authorization\n3. **Response**: `\"PAYMENT-RESPONSE\"` - server to client with settlement outcome\n\n## Encoding\n\n`\"All headers contain valid Base64-encoded JSON strings. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XKFs7p9u3FbFS4yN76r1rj","type":"tool_result","content":"# Bazaar Discovery Layer Overview\n\n## What It Is\n\nThe Bazaar functions as a machine-readable catalog enabling developers and AI agents to autonomously locate and integrate x402-compatible API endpoints and MCP tools. It addresses the critical challenge of service discoverability in the x402 ecosystem.\n\n## Operator\n\nThe documentation does not explicitly identify who operates the Bazaar. It references facilitators as entities that \"support the Bazaar extension\" and \"may provide a `/discovery/resources` endpoint,\" suggesting facilitators are responsible parties, though the relationship between facilitators and Bazaar operation remains implicit.\n\n## Resource Server Listing\n\nListing occurs **automatically through facilitators**—no explicit registration step is required. Resources become discoverable when:\n\n1. Service operators \"include the bazaar extension in their route configuration\"\n2. A client pays for the service while echoing the bazaar extension in the PaymentPayload\n3. The facilitator validates and catalogs the declaration\n\nAs the documentation cautions: \"Payment verification and settlement succeeding does not, by itself, guarantee catalog inclusion.\"\n\n## Discovery API Endpoint\n\n```\nGET {facilitator_url}/discovery/resources\n```\n\nThis endpoint retrieves all x402-compatible services from facilitators supporting Bazaar discovery. Clients can filter by resource type (`http` or `mcp`) and implement search functionality via natural-language queries where supported."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"ab8f4148-da44-4e0e-96b6-22dbf881a311","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:29:12.299Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":37682,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# Bazaar Discovery Layer Overview\n\n## What It Is\n\nThe Bazaar functions as a machine-readable catalog enabling developers and AI agents to autonomously locate and integrate x402-compatible API endpoints and MCP tools. It addresses the critical challenge of service discoverability in the x402 ecosystem.\n\n## Operator\n\nThe documentation does not explicitly identify who operates the Bazaar. It references facilitators as entities that \"support the Bazaar extension\" and \"may provide a `/discovery/resources` endpoint,\" suggesting facilitators are responsible parties, though the relationship between facilitators and Bazaar operation remains implicit.\n\n## Resource Server Listing\n\nListing occurs **automatically through facilitators**—no explicit registration step is required. Resources become discoverable when:\n\n1. Service operators \"include the bazaar extension in their route configuration\"\n2. A client pays for the service while echoing the bazaar extension in the PaymentPayload\n3. The facilitator validates and catalogs the declaration\n\nAs the documentation cautions: \"Payment verification and settlement succeeding does not, by itself, guarantee catalog inclusion.\"\n\n## Discovery API Endpoint\n\n```\nGET {facilitator_url}/discovery/resources\n```\n\nThis endpoint retrieves all x402-compatible services from facilitators supporting Bazaar discovery. Clients can filter by resource type (`http` or `mcp`) and implement search functionality via natural-language queries where supported.","durationMs":5092,"url":"https://docs.x402.org/extensions/bazaar.md"}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01D9x1AkrXfsHdK3VZojcsgq","type":"tool_result","content":"# X402 Protocol Field Reference\n\n## `resource` Object (PaymentRequired)\nThe ResourceInfo object contains three fields:\n- `url` (string, required)\n- `description` (string, optional)\n- `mimeType` (string, optional)\n\n## PaymentRequirements Fields\n- `scheme` (string, required)\n- `network` (string, required)\n- `amount` (string, required)\n- `asset` (string, required)\n- `payTo` (string, required)\n- `maxTimeoutSeconds` (number, required)\n- `extra` (object, optional)\n\n## Facilitator `/verify` Endpoint\n\n**Request fields:**\n- `x402Version`\n- `paymentPayload`\n- `paymentRequirements`\n\n**Response fields:**\n- `isValid` (boolean, required)\n- `invalidReason` (string, optional)\n- `payer` (string, optional)\n\n## Facilitator `/settle` Endpoint\n\n**Request fields:**\nSame as `/verify` (identical structure)\n\n**Response fields:**\n- `success` (boolean, required)\n- `errorReason` (string, optional)\n- `payer` (string, optional)\n- `transaction` (string, required)\n- `network` (string, required)\n- `amount` (string, optional)\n- `extensions` (object, optional)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"7e80d084-dfd7-4b8c-a7b1-aab760b8d31e","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:29:28.884Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":31299,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# `paymentRequirements`\n\n**Response fields:**\n- `isValid` (boolean, required)\n- `invalidReason` (string, optional)\n- `payer` (string, optional)\n\n## Facilitator `/settle` Endpoint\n\n**Request fields:**\nSame as `/verify` (identical structure)\n\n**Response fields:**\n- `success` (boolean, required)\n- `errorReason` (string, optional)\n- `payer` (string, optional)\n- `transaction` (string, required)\n- `network` (string, required)\n- `amount` (string, optional)\n- `extensions` (object, {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeRuwe2WdmpE3hFCkkM7L","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017uXxcGuDiKb15A9AdsPnxF","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > design.md <<'DESIGN_EOF'\n# forecast.example.com — service-side design\n\nSells a single product: a point weather forecast, **$0.35 per call**, paid in **USDC on\nBase (chain 8453)**. No accounts, no API keys, no invoices, no human in any step.\n\nThe design is an assembly of four existing standards. Nothing here is bespoke protocol:\n\n| Constraint | Mechanism |\n|---|---|\n| Cold discovery, no catalog we own | **ERC-8004 Identity Registry** on Base + a registration file at a well-known URL, bound to each other in both directions |\n| Judge trustworthiness before first call | **ERC-8004 Reputation Registry** reads + proof-of-payment-filtered feedback |\n| Per-call billing, no accounts/keys | **x402** (HTTP 402 challenge → signed payment → settle → 200) |\n| Caller holds USDC but no ETH | **EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization`**, broadcast and gas-paid by an **x402 facilitator** |\n| Caller can rate us afterwards | `ReputationRegistry.giveFeedback(...)`, called by the client, readable by everyone |\n| No humans | Every artifact above is machine-readable JSON or an onchain call |\n\n---\n\n## 1. End-to-end flow (client has never heard of us)\n\n```\n                                   Base mainnet (8453)\n  ┌────────────┐            ┌───────────────────────────────────┐\n  │ client     │  (1) scan  │ IdentityRegistry  0x8004A1…a432   │\n  │ agent      │───────────▶│   agentId 7412 → agentURI         │\n  │ (USDC,     │  (2) read  │ ReputationRegistry 0x8004BA…9b63  │\n  │  no ETH)   │───────────▶│   getSummary(7412, …)             │\n  └─────┬──────┘            └───────────────────────────────────┘\n        │ (3) GET /.well-known/agent-registration.json   (free, TLS)\n        │ (4) GET /forecast?lat=…&lon=…      →  402 + PaymentRequired\n        │ (5) sign EIP-3009 authorization (offline, costs no gas)\n        │ (6) GET /forecast … + PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header\n        ▼\n  ┌────────────┐  verify/settle   ┌──────────────┐  transferWithAuthorization\n  │ forecast   │─────────────────▶│ x402         │──────────────────────────▶ USDC\n  │ server     │◀─────────────────│ facilitator  │   (facilitator pays the gas)\n  └─────┬──────┘   txHash, payer  └──────────────┘\n        │ (7) 200 + forecast + PAYMENT-RESPONSE (txHash) + feedback pointer\n        ▼\n  (8) client calls ReputationRegistry.giveFeedback(7412, 5, 0, \"forecast\", …,\n      feedbackURI → JSON containing proofOfPayment{chainId, txHash, from, to})\n```\n\nSteps 1–3 need no payment and no permission. Step 5 needs no ETH: EIP-3009 is a plain\nEIP-712 signature. Step 8 is the only step where the client itself sends a transaction —\nsee §5 for how a client that owns literally zero ETH still leaves a rating.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Discovery and identity\n\n### 2.1 Onchain anchor — ERC-8004 Identity Registry\n\nWe mint one agent identity in the **shared, public** ERC-8004 Identity Registry on Base.\nIt is an ERC-721: `agentId` is the token id, the token owner is our operator key, and the\ntoken's `agentURI` points at our registration file.\n\n```solidity\nregister(\"https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/agent-registration.json\",\n         [ MetadataEntry(\"x402.payTo\",   bytes(\"0x…payTo\")),\n           MetadataEntry(\"x402.asset\",   bytes(\"eip155:8453/erc20:0x8335…2913\")),\n           MetadataEntry(\"x402.price\",   bytes(\"350000\")) ])   // 6-dec USDC atomic\n→ agentId\n```\n\nWe do not own or operate this registry, and anyone can enumerate it: `Registered`,\n`URIUpdated` and `MetadataSet` events are public, so any client, indexer, subgraph or\nblock explorer can find us without our cooperation. Discovery therefore survives us\ngoing offline, losing a domain, or refusing to list a competitor — none of which we\ncould do anyway.\n\n### 2.2 Offchain half — the registration file\n\nServed at `https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/agent-registration.json`\n(also the exact string stored as `agentURI` onchain):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1\",\n  \"name\": \"forecast.example.com\",\n  \"description\": \"Point weather forecasts for any lat/lon, 0.35 USDC per call, no account required.\",\n  \"image\": \"https://forecast.example.com/static/icon.png\",\n  \"services\": [\n    { \"name\": \"web\",  \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/\" },\n    { \"name\": \"HTTP\", \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/openapi.json\", \"version\": \"3.1.0\" }\n  ],\n  \"x402Support\": true,\n  \"active\": true,\n  \"registrations\": [\n    { \"agentId\": 7412, \"agentRegistry\": \"eip155:8453:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432\" }\n  ],\n  \"supportedTrust\": [\"reputation\"],\n  \"x402\": {\n    \"network\": \"eip155:8453\",\n    \"asset\": \"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\",\n    \"payTo\": \"0x…payTo\",\n    \"endpoints\": [{ \"method\": \"GET\", \"path\": \"/forecast\", \"amount\": \"350000\", \"scheme\": \"exact\" }]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 2.3 The binding is bidirectional, and that is the point\n\n* **Chain → domain**: the onchain `agentURI` names the host. Fetching it over TLS proves\n  the identity refers to the host a valid certificate was issued for.\n* **Domain → chain**: the file's `registrations[]` names the `agentId` **and** the exact\n  registry contract it must live in.\n\nA client accepts the identity only if both directions agree with where it started. If\nsomeone re-publishes our file on `evil.example`, direction 1 fails (the onchain URI still\nsays `forecast.example.com`). If someone registers a *new* agentId pointing at our URL,\ndirection 2 fails (our file lists 7412, not theirs) — so they cannot inherit our ratings.\nTwo lines of JSON carry the whole anti-impersonation property; getting either one wrong\nsilently breaks it, which is why the server generates the file from the same config that\ndrives payment (`server.ts`, `registrationFile()`).\n\nOptional hardening, both machine-checkable: `setAgentWallet(agentId, payTo, …)` so the\n`payTo` in our 402 challenge can be checked against the chain (a MITM cannot redirect\npayment to itself), and a DNS `TXT _erc8004.forecast.example.com = \"agentId=7412;\nregistry=eip155:8453:0x8004A1…\"` for clients that start from a hostname.\n\n### 2.4 What we deliberately do not do\n\nWe publish no catalog and run no directory. The *only* thing a stranger must reach to\nfind us is a public contract on Base. Third-party indexes (x402 Bazaar, ERC-8004\nexplorers, any subgraph) are welcome mirrors — none is load-bearing, and we can be listed\nin them without asking us.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Judging us before the first call — the trust path\n\nEverything a client needs is free and unauthenticated:\n\n1. **Identity is real and ours** — §2.3 binding check.\n2. **Age and history** — block number of the `Registered` event; `URIUpdated` churn.\n3. **Ratings** — `ReputationRegistry.getSummary(7412, [], \"forecast\", \"\")` returns\n   `(count, summaryValue, summaryValueDecimals)`; `readAllFeedback(...)` returns the\n   individual scores with their client addresses, and `getClients(7412)` the raters.\n4. **Sybil filtering (this is the important part)** — ERC-8004 lets *anyone* call\n   `giveFeedback`; the registry is a bulletin board, not an oracle. So a rating is only\n   worth acting on if it carries evidence. Each of our receipts tells the client to write\n   a `feedbackURI` file containing:\n\n   ```json\n   { \"agentRegistry\": \"eip155:8453:0x8004A1…\", \"agentId\": 7412,\n     \"clientAddress\": \"0x…\", \"createdAt\": \"2026-08-26T19:26:19Z\",\n     \"value\": 5, \"valueDecimals\": 0, \"tag1\": \"forecast\", \"tag2\": \"latency\",\n     \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/forecast\",\n     \"proofOfPayment\": { \"chainId\": 8453, \"txHash\": \"0x…\",\n                         \"fromAddress\": \"0x…client\", \"toAddress\": \"0x…payTo\" } }\n   ```\n\n   A reader fetches that file, hashes it against the onchain `feedbackHash`, then checks\n   on Base that `txHash` really is a USDC transfer of 350000 from `clientAddress` to our\n   `payTo`. Ratings that fail that check are noise; ratings that pass cost $0.35 each to\n   forge, and the forgery pays *us*. That converts an open registry into a\n   payment-gated one without any permissioning.\n5. **Price honesty** — an unpaid `GET /forecast` returns the 402 challenge for free, so\n   the advertised price can be compared with the registration file and the onchain\n   metadata before spending anything.\n6. **Response quality, pre-purchase** — `/openapi.json` carries the exact response\n   schema, and `GET /forecast/sample` returns a fixed, unpaid example response.\n\nWe do **not** serve our own aggregate rating as an authority. `/.well-known/reputation.json`\nexists, but it only tells the client *where and how to read the chain itself* (registry\naddress, agentId, recommended tag filters, the feedback-file template above). A vendor\nreporting its own score is worthless; a vendor telling you exactly how to compute it\nyourself is not.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Payment — x402 + EIP-3009\n\n### 4.1 Wire flow\n\n`GET /forecast?lat=52.52&lon=13.405` with no payment header → **402** with the\n`PaymentRequired` object in the body *and* base64 in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header:\n\n```json\n{ \"x402Version\": 2,\n  \"resource\": { \"url\": \"https://forecast.example.com/forecast\",\n                \"description\": \"48h point weather forecast\", \"mimeType\": \"application/json\" },\n  \"accepts\": [\n    { \"scheme\": \"exact\", \"network\": \"eip155:8453\", \"amount\": \"350000\",\n      \"asset\": \"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\",\n      \"payTo\": \"0x…payTo\", \"maxTimeoutSeconds\": 90,\n      \"extra\": { \"name\": \"USD Coin\", \"version\": \"2\", \"assetTransferMethod\": \"eip3009\" } }\n  ],\n  \"extensions\": {} }\n```\n\nThe client signs an EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization` (EIP-712 domain\n`{name:\"USD Coin\", version:\"2\", chainId:8453, verifyingContract:USDC}`) and retries with\n`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: base64({x402Version, accepted, payload:{signature, authorization:{from,to,value,validAfter,validBefore,nonce}}})`.\n\nServer: local sanity checks → facilitator `POST /verify` → produce the forecast →\nfacilitator `POST /settle` → **200** with the data, `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (base64 settle\nresult, incl. `transaction`) and a `feedback` block in the body.\n\n`amount` is `\"350000\"` — 0.35 × 10⁶, USDC has 6 decimals. The price is a fixed atomic\ninteger, not a float, and not a USD lookup: we sell for 0.35 USDC and let the client\ndecide what that is worth.\n\n### 4.2 Why the caller needs no ETH\n\nEIP-3009 is the entire answer. The client's signature is produced offline and costs\nnothing; the **facilitator** submits `transferWithAuthorization` to USDC and pays the Base\ngas. Value moves client → us in one transaction the client never has to broadcast.\n\n* The facilitator **cannot steal**: `to`, `value`, `validBefore` and `nonce` are inside\n  the signed EIP-712 payload. It can only broadcast that exact transfer, or nothing.\n* Clients that are smart accounts and cannot produce a raw EOA signature are covered by\n  the same scheme via EIP-1271/ERC-6492 signature validation, or by the Permit2 /\n  ERC-7710 transfer methods in the x402 exact scheme — advertise a second `accepts`\n  entry if that traffic matters. (Permit2 needs a one-off approval tx, which *does* cost\n  the client gas; EIP-3009 stays the zero-ETH path and is the one we advertise first.)\n* We never need ETH either, for anything except the one-time registry writes in §7.\n\n### 4.3 Ordering, replay and idempotency\n\n* **verify → work → settle.** Verify first so we never burn an upstream call on an\n  invalid payment; settle last so we never charge for a forecast we failed to produce.\n  The residual risk is a settle failure *after* we've done the work: we eat the upstream\n  cost and return 502 with no charge. That is the correct side to fail on.\n* **Replay.** The authorization `nonce` is single-use in USDC itself, so a replay can\n  never double-charge onchain — but it could double-*serve*. We keep a nonce table:\n  in-flight nonces are locked, and settled nonces map to the cached response.\n* **Idempotency.** A client whose connection drops after we settled retries with the same\n  authorization and gets the same forecast from cache instead of a \"nonce already used\"\n  error. Without this, every dropped TCP connection is a $0.35 loss and a 1-star rating.\n* **Expiry.** We reject `validBefore` closer than a settlement buffer (~15s) so the\n  authorization cannot expire between `/verify` and `/settle`.\n* **Binding.** Before settling we re-check `authorization.to == payTo`,\n  `value == 350000`, and asset/network/scheme against our own requirements, and pass our\n  own `paymentRequirements` to the facilitator so it enforces them too.\n\n---\n\n## 5. The rating loop\n\nThe 200 response carries everything needed to rate us, so the client needs no docs:\n\n```json\n\"feedback\": {\n  \"registry\": \"eip155:8453:0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63\",\n  \"agentId\": 7412,\n  \"method\": \"giveFeedback(uint256,int128,uint8,string,string,string,string,bytes32)\",\n  \"suggested\": { \"tag1\": \"forecast\", \"tag2\": \"latency\", \"valueDecimals\": 0, \"range\": [0, 5] },\n  \"endpoint\": \"https://forecast.example.com/forecast\",\n  \"proofOfPayment\": { \"chainId\": 8453, \"txHash\": \"0x…\", \"fromAddress\": \"0x…\", \"toAddress\": \"0x…payTo\" },\n  \"feedbackFileTemplate\": \"https://forecast.example.com/.well-known/reputation.json\"\n}\n```\n\nThe client uploads its feedback file (IPFS, its own host, anywhere addressable), then\ncalls `giveFeedback(7412, value, 0, \"forecast\", \"latency\", endpoint, feedbackURI,\nfeedbackHash)`. The rating lives in a contract we do not control: we cannot delete it,\nand `revokeFeedback` is the *client's* to call, not ours. Our only recourse is\n`appendResponse(...)` — a public reply, which is the honest remedy.\n\n**The zero-ETH client rates us too.** `giveFeedback` is a normal transaction, so a client\nwith no ETH would be stuck at the last step. Three machine-only outs, in order of\npreference: (a) the client's account abstraction wallet uses a paymaster that accepts\nUSDC — the common case for agent wallets in practice; (b) it batches ratings and sends\none transaction per N calls; (c) it swaps a few cents of USDC for ETH. This is a real\nconstraint on the client side and we should not pretend x402 solves it — what we *can*\ndo, and do, is make the rating call cost one transaction with no approvals, no\nregistration, and no interaction with us.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Dependencies\n\n### 6.1 Onchain (all on Base mainnet, chain 8453)\n\n| Dependency | Address | Used for | If it fails |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Base L2 (sequencer) | chain 8453 | settlement | payments stall; verify still works, we can serve on credit or return 503 |\n| USDC | `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913` | the money; EIP-3009 | Circle can freeze addresses — ours or a client's — and pauses are possible |\n| ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry | `0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432` | discovery, identity | already-registered clients keep working; new cold discovery breaks |\n| ERC-8004 ReputationRegistry | `0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63` | ratings | trust signal freezes; payments unaffected |\n| Permit2 (optional) | `0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3` | non-3009 assets / smart accounts | only affects the fallback path |\n| ValidationRegistry | not pinned | optional crypto-economic / TEE trust | unused today; the ERC's validation half is still in flux |\n\n**Verify the two registry addresses onchain before deploying.** They are the Base-mainnet\ndeployments published by the ERC-8004 contracts repo; a service that hardcodes a wrong\nregistry is discoverable by nobody and rateable by nobody. Treat them as config\n(`IDENTITY_REGISTRY`, `REPUTATION_REGISTRY`), not constants.\n\nWe are **not** onchain ourselves: no contract of ours is deployed, no funds are custodied,\nno state of ours lives on Base except one ERC-721 and whatever clients say about us.\n\n### 6.2 Offchain\n\n| Dependency | Role | Trust we place in it | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| x402 facilitator (CDP, Mogami, Corbits, or self-hosted) | verify + broadcast + pay gas | liveness only — it cannot alter `to`/`value`/`nonce` | configure a primary + fallback URL; self-hosting is a signer and an RPC, nothing more |\n| Base RPC provider | registry writes/reads, facilitator's own settlement | liveness, correct view of chain | two providers; clients use their own |\n| DNS + CA (TLS) | domain half of the identity binding | a mis-issued cert forges the offchain half | CAA records, HSTS, cert transparency monitoring; the onchain half still has to match |\n| Weather data upstream (Open-Meteo by default) | the actual product | correctness of what we sell — this is what ratings measure | multi-source, cache, fail closed (502, no settle) rather than serve garbage |\n| Feedback file hosting | client-side, not ours | none | we only need the URI to resolve at read time |\n| Indexers / subgraphs / Bazaar | convenience discovery | none — mirrors of public logs | anyone can rebuild from Base logs |\n| Key custody | `payTo` receives; owner key writes to the registry | funds and identity | `payTo` = cold multisig (receive-only, no hot key needed since we never sign transfers); owner key offline, used ~once |\n\nNotably absent: no database of users, no auth service, no billing/invoicing system, no\npayment processor, no KYC of clients, and no custody of client funds — per-call x402\ndeletes that entire subsystem. (A CDP-style facilitator does apply KYT/OFAC screening to\nsettlement, which is worth knowing before choosing one.)\n\n---\n\n## 7. What we must publish, and what we must register\n\n### Publish (all served by `server.ts`, all unauthenticated)\n\n| URL | Content |\n|---|---|\n| `/.well-known/agent-registration.json` | ERC-8004 registration file (§2.2). Must byte-for-byte satisfy the onchain `agentURI` and carry the right `agentId`. |\n| `/.well-known/reputation.json` | Where/how to read our ratings and how to leave one: registry, agentId, tags, feedback-file template. |\n| `/.well-known/x402` | Machine-readable list of priced routes (convention, not a spec — a hint for crawlers). |\n| `/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 for `/forecast`, including the 402 response and payment headers. |\n| `/forecast/sample` | Free, fixed sample response so quality can be judged before paying. |\n| `/` | JSON index linking all of the above. |\n| DNS `TXT _erc8004` (optional) | hostname → agentId hint. |\n\n### Register (once, before anyone can find us)\n\n1. DNS + TLS certificate for `forecast.example.com`.\n2. Deploy the server; the registration file must resolve **before** step 4 (the URI is\n   fetched by clients the moment we appear onchain).\n3. Fund the owner EOA with a small amount of ETH on Base — the only ETH this business\n   ever needs, ~2 transactions' worth.\n4. `IdentityRegistry.register(agentURI, metadata)` → returns `agentId`.\n5. Write the returned `agentId` into the registration file and redeploy (`AGENT_ID` env).\n   **Until this lands, the binding is one-directional and a careful client will refuse us.**\n6. Optional: `setAgentWallet(agentId, payTo, deadline, sig)`; the DNS TXT record; ENS name.\n7. Optional: enable the x402 Bazaar extension so facilitators catalog the route — pure\n   upside, zero dependency.\n\nNot required, at all: signing up with any marketplace, obtaining an API key from anyone,\nlisting in a directory, or a human approving anything.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Failure modes worth stating\n\n* **Facilitator down** → 503 with `Retry-After`; no client funds are ever in flight, since\n  settlement is atomic and pre-verified.\n* **Settle succeeds, response lost** → idempotent replay from the nonce cache (§4.3).\n* **Upstream weather API down** → 502 before settle; the client is not charged.\n* **Client underpays / wrong network / expired auth** → 402 again with the correct\n  `accepts`, not an error page. Every failure returns the machine-actionable next step.\n* **Price change** → new challenges quote the new amount immediately; in-flight signed\n  authorizations at the old price are still honoured until `validBefore` (they were\n  signed against a challenge we issued). Never settle an authorization for *less* than\n  the current advertised price without serving it — that is a rating we deserve to lose.\n* **Sybil ratings against us** → competitors can post fake 1-stars for free. The\n  proof-of-payment convention in §3 is what makes them ignorable; we should publish the\n  filtering rule (we do, in `/.well-known/reputation.json`) rather than complain about it.\n* **USDC blacklists `payTo`** → payments revert at settle; rotate `payTo`, update onchain\n  metadata + registration file.\n\n## 9. Running it\n\n```bash\nexport PAY_TO_ADDRESS=0x…                 # cold receive-only address\nexport AGENT_ID=7412                      # from IdentityRegistry.register\nexport FACILITATOR_URL=https://api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402\nexport FACILITATOR_API_KEY=…              # if the facilitator requires one\nnode --experimental-strip-types server.ts # Node >= 22.6, or: npx tsx server.ts\n```\n\n`server.ts` holds no private key, touches no RPC, and stores nothing but a short-lived\nnonce cache. Everything that needs a key is either the client's problem (signing the\nauthorization), the facilitator's (broadcasting), or a one-time offline operation (the\nregistry writes).\nDESIGN_EOF\nwc -l design.md","description":"Write design.md"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":632,"cache_read_input_tokens":44720,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":632},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"0a5b72be-5ec6-4666-9d20-81c4cc44a479","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:33:27.557Z","request_id":"req_011CeRuwdFPBZLwKYGFeEq7C"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeRvFEbrodWKBoZpNEjRg","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_015F2rFsh6C1nbhY1yce4WpB","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > server.ts <<'SERVER_EOF'\n/**\n * forecast.example.com — service side.\n *\n * Sells one product: a 48h point forecast, 0.35 USDC on Base, per call, x402.\n * No accounts, no API keys, no balances. See design.md.\n *\n * Deliberately dependency-free (node: builtins + fetch only):\n *  - it holds no private key,\n *  - it never talks to an RPC node (the facilitator does the chain work),\n *  - its only state is a short-lived nonce cache for replay/idempotency.\n *\n * Run: node --experimental-strip-types server.ts   (Node >= 22.6)\n */\n\nimport http from \"node:http\";\nimport { URL } from \"node:url\";\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Config. Everything that could ever differ per deployment lives here — most\n// importantly the registry addresses, which must be verified onchain and never\n// treated as constants.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst cfg = {\n  port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8402),\n  origin: process.env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN ?? \"https://forecast.example.com\",\n\n  // Money\n  payTo: process.env.PAY_TO_ADDRESS ?? \"\",\n  priceAtomic: process.env.PRICE_ATOMIC ?? \"350000\", // 0.35 USDC, 6 decimals\n  asset: process.env.USDC_ADDRESS ?? \"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\",\n  assetName: process.env.USDC_EIP712_NAME ?? \"USD Coin\", // EIP-712 domain, EIP-3009\n  assetVersion: process.env.USDC_EIP712_VERSION ?? \"2\",\n  chainId: Number(process.env.CHAIN_ID ?? 8453), // Base mainnet\n  networkCaip2: `eip155:${process.env.CHAIN_ID ?? 8453}`,\n  networkLegacy: process.env.NETWORK_LEGACY ?? \"base\", // x402 v1 network name\n\n  // Identity / reputation (ERC-8004, Base mainnet) — verify onchain before deploy.\n  agentId: process.env.AGENT_ID ?? \"\",\n  identityRegistry: process.env.IDENTITY_REGISTRY ?? \"0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432\",\n  reputationRegistry: process.env.REPUTATION_REGISTRY ?? \"0x8004BAa17C55a88189AE136b182e5fdA19dE9b63\",\n\n  // Facilitator: verifies signatures, broadcasts transferWithAuthorization,\n  // pays the Base gas. It cannot alter to/value/nonce — those are signed.\n  facilitatorUrl: (process.env.FACILITATOR_URL ?? \"https://x402.org/facilitator\").replace(/\\/$/, \"\"),\n  facilitatorApiKey: process.env.FACILITATOR_API_KEY ?? \"\",\n\n  upstreamUrl: process.env.UPSTREAM_URL ?? \"https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast\",\n\n  maxTimeoutSeconds: 90,\n  settleBufferSeconds: 15, // reject authorizations that could expire mid-settle\n  idempotencyTtlMs: 10 * 60 * 1000,\n};\n\nconst RESOURCE_URL = `${cfg.origin}/forecast`;\nconst AGENT_REGISTRY_CAIP = `${cfg.networkCaip2}:${cfg.identityRegistry}`;\nconst REPUTATION_REGISTRY_CAIP = `${cfg.networkCaip2}:${cfg.reputationRegistry}`;\n\nfunction assertConfig(): void {\n  const missing: string[] = [];\n  if (!/^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$/.test(cfg.payTo)) missing.push(\"PAY_TO_ADDRESS (0x-address that receives USDC)\");\n  if (!/^\\d+$/.test(cfg.agentId)) missing.push(\"AGENT_ID (uint from IdentityRegistry.register)\");\n  if (missing.length) {\n    console.error(`refusing to start, missing config:\\n  - ${missing.join(\"\\n  - \")}`);\n    console.error(\"AGENT_ID is not optional: without it the registration file cannot bind back to the\");\n    console.error(\"onchain identity, and a careful client will (correctly) refuse to trust this service.\");\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Small helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ntype Json = Record<string, unknown>;\n\nconst b64encode = (o: unknown) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(o), \"utf8\").toString(\"base64\");\n\nfunction b64decode(raw: string): Json | null {\n  try {\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(raw.trim(), \"base64\").toString(\"utf8\"));\n    return parsed && typeof parsed === \"object\" ? (parsed as Json) : null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction send(res: http.ServerResponse, status: number, body: unknown, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): void {\n  const payload = typeof body === \"string\" ? body : JSON.stringify(body, null, 2);\n  res.writeHead(status, {\n    \"content-type\": \"application/json; charset=utf-8\",\n    \"cache-control\": \"no-store\",\n    \"access-control-allow-origin\": \"*\",\n    \"access-control-expose-headers\": \"PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-RESPONSE, X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE\",\n    ...headers,\n  });\n  res.end(payload);\n}\n\n/** Same network, written two ways (\"base\" vs \"eip155:8453\"). */\nconst sameNetwork = (a: string, b: string) => norm(a) === norm(b);\nconst norm = (n: string) => (n === cfg.networkLegacy ? cfg.networkCaip2 : String(n).toLowerCase());\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// x402: payment requirements\n//\n// We publish two `accepts` entries that differ only in how the network is\n// spelled, and each entry carries both the v2 field (`amount`) and the v1 alias\n// (`maxAmountRequired`). x402 v2 renamed these; agents in the wild speak both.\n// Supersets are cheap, a client that cannot parse our challenge is a lost sale.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfunction requirementsFor(network: string): Json {\n  return {\n    scheme: \"exact\",\n    network,\n    amount: cfg.priceAtomic, // x402 v2\n    maxAmountRequired: cfg.priceAtomic, // x402 v1 alias\n    asset: cfg.asset,\n    payTo: cfg.payTo,\n    maxTimeoutSeconds: cfg.maxTimeoutSeconds,\n    resource: RESOURCE_URL,\n    description: \"48h point weather forecast for one lat/lon\",\n    mimeType: \"application/json\",\n    extra: {\n      // EIP-712 domain of the USDC contract, needed to sign EIP-3009.\n      name: cfg.assetName,\n      version: cfg.assetVersion,\n      assetTransferMethod: \"eip3009\",\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nconst ACCEPTS = [requirementsFor(cfg.networkCaip2), requirementsFor(cfg.networkLegacy)];\n\nfunction paymentRequired(error: string): Json {\n  return {\n    x402Version: 2,\n    x402VersionsSupported: [1, 2],\n    error,\n    resource: {\n      url: RESOURCE_URL,\n      description: \"48h point weather forecast for one lat/lon\",\n      mimeType: \"application/json\",\n    },\n    accepts: ACCEPTS,\n    extensions: {},\n  };\n}\n\nfunction sendChallenge(res: http.ServerResponse, error: string): void {\n  const body = paymentRequired(error);\n  send(res, 402, body, { \"PAYMENT-REQUIRED\": b64encode(body) });\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// x402: reading the client's payment\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ntype Parsed = {\n  version: number;\n  payload: Json;\n  authorization: Json;\n  requirements: Json;\n  nonce: string;\n};\n\nfunction parsePayment(req: http.IncomingMessage): { ok: true; value: Parsed } | { ok: false; error: string } {\n  const header =\n    (req.headers[\"payment-signature\"] as string | undefined) ?? // x402 v2\n    (req.headers[\"x-payment\"] as string | undefined); // x402 v1\n  if (!header) return { ok: false, error: \"PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header is required\" };\n\n  const decoded = b64decode(header);\n  if (!decoded) return { ok: false, error: \"payment header is not base64-encoded JSON\" };\n\n  const version = Number(decoded.x402Version ?? 1);\n  if (version !== 1 && version !== 2) return { ok: false, error: `unsupported x402Version ${version}` };\n\n  const accepted = (decoded.accepted ?? {}) as Json; // v2 echoes the chosen requirements\n  const scheme = String(decoded.scheme ?? accepted.scheme ?? \"\");\n  const network = String(decoded.network ?? accepted.network ?? \"\");\n  if (scheme !== \"exact\") return { ok: false, error: `unsupported scheme \"${scheme}\", this resource accepts \"exact\"` };\n\n  const requirements = ACCEPTS.find((r) => sameNetwork(String(r.network), network));\n  if (!requirements) return { ok: false, error: `unsupported network \"${network}\"` };\n\n  const payload = (decoded.payload ?? {}) as Json;\n  const authorization = (payload.authorization ?? {}) as Json;\n  if (!payload.signature || !authorization.nonce) {\n    return { ok: false, error: \"payload must contain an EIP-3009 signature and authorization\" };\n  }\n\n  // Local pre-checks. The facilitator re-verifies all of this against the chain,\n  // but rejecting here is free and keeps obviously-wrong payments off its budget.\n  if (String(authorization.to).toLowerCase() !== cfg.payTo.toLowerCase()) {\n    return { ok: false, error: `authorization.to must be ${cfg.payTo}` };\n  }\n  if (String(authorization.value) !== cfg.priceAtomic) {\n    return { ok: false, error: `authorization.value must be exactly ${cfg.priceAtomic} (0.35 USDC)` };\n  }\n  const asset = String(accepted.asset ?? decoded.asset ?? cfg.asset).toLowerCase();\n  if (asset !== cfg.asset.toLowerCase()) return { ok: false, error: `unsupported asset ${asset}` };\n\n  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);\n  const validBefore = Number(authorization.validBefore ?? 0);\n  const validAfter = Number(authorization.validAfter ?? 0);\n  if (validAfter > now) return { ok: false, error: \"authorization is not valid yet\" };\n  if (validBefore <= now + cfg.settleBufferSeconds) {\n    return { ok: false, error: `authorization expires too soon, need validBefore > now + ${cfg.settleBufferSeconds}s` };\n  }\n\n  return {\n    ok: true,\n    value: {\n      version,\n      payload: decoded,\n      authorization,\n      requirements,\n      nonce: String(authorization.nonce).toLowerCase(),\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Facilitator client. Liveness dependency only: it can refuse to settle, it\n// cannot redirect or resize a payment — to/value/nonce are inside the signature.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nasync function facilitator(path: \"verify\" | \"settle\", p: Parsed): Promise<Json> {\n  const headers: Record<string, string> = { \"content-type\": \"application/json\" };\n  if (cfg.facilitatorApiKey) headers.authorization = `Bearer ${cfg.facilitatorApiKey}`;\n\n  const controller = new AbortController();\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), cfg.maxTimeoutSeconds * 1000);\n  try {\n    const resp = await fetch(`${cfg.facilitatorUrl}/${path}`, {\n      method: \"POST\",\n      headers,\n      signal: controller.signal,\n      body: JSON.stringify({\n        x402Version: p.version,\n        paymentPayload: p.payload,\n        paymentRequirements: p.requirements, // our terms, enforced facilitator-side too\n      }),\n    });\n    const text = await resp.text();\n    const json = text ? (JSON.parse(text) as Json) : {};\n    if (!resp.ok) return { ...json, _httpStatus: resp.status, _transport: `facilitator ${path} returned ${resp.status}` };\n    return json;\n  } catch (err) {\n    return { _transport: `facilitator ${path} unreachable: ${(err as Error).message}` };\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Nonce table: replay protection + idempotency.\n//\n// USDC itself makes an EIP-3009 nonce single-use, so a replay can never\n// double-charge onchain. What it could do is double-serve, or — worse for the\n// client — make an honest retry after a dropped connection look like a replay\n// and cost them $0.35 for nothing. So: in-flight nonces are locked, settled\n// nonces replay their cached response.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ntype Entry =\n  | { state: \"pending\"; expiresAt: number }\n  | { state: \"settled\"; expiresAt: number; body: Json; settleHeader: string };\n\nconst nonces = new Map<string, Entry>();\n\nsetInterval(() => {\n  const now = Date.now();\n  for (const [k, v] of nonces) if (v.expiresAt <= now) nonces.delete(k);\n}, 60_000).unref();\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// The product\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ntype Forecast = Json;\n\nasync function buildForecast(lat: number, lon: number, hours: number): Promise<Forecast> {\n  const url = new URL(cfg.upstreamUrl);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"latitude\", String(lat));\n  url.searchParams.set(\"longitude\", String(lon));\n  url.searchParams.set(\"hourly\", \"temperature_2m,precipitation_probability,wind_speed_10m,weather_code\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"forecast_hours\", String(hours));\n  url.searchParams.set(\"timezone\", \"UTC\");\n\n  const resp = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) });\n  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`upstream ${resp.status}`);\n  const raw = (await resp.json()) as any;\n  const h = raw.hourly ?? {};\n  const times: string[] = h.time ?? [];\n\n  return {\n    location: { lat, lon, timezone: \"UTC\" },\n    generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),\n    units: { temperature: \"C\", precipitationProbability: \"%\", windSpeed: \"km/h\" },\n    hourly: times.map((t, i) => ({\n      time: t,\n      temperature: h.temperature_2m?.[i] ?? null,\n      precipitationProbability: h.precipitation_probability?.[i] ?? null,\n      windSpeed: h.wind_speed_10m?.[i] ?? null,\n      weatherCode: h.weather_code?.[i] ?? null,\n    })),\n  };\n}\n\n/** Everything the caller needs to rate us, so it never has to read documentation. */\nfunction feedbackBlock(settlement: Json, payer: string): Json {\n  return {\n    registry: REPUTATION_REGISTRY_CAIP,\n    agentId: Number(cfg.agentId),\n    method: \"giveFeedback(uint256,int128,uint8,string,string,string,string,bytes32)\",\n    suggested: { tag1: \"forecast\", tag2: \"latency\", valueDecimals: 0, range: [0, 5] },\n    endpoint: RESOURCE_URL,\n    proofOfPayment: {\n      chainId: cfg.chainId,\n      txHash: settlement.transaction ?? null,\n      fromAddress: payer || null,\n      toAddress: cfg.payTo,\n    },\n    feedbackFileTemplate: `${cfg.origin}/.well-known/reputation.json`,\n    note:\n      \"Publish the feedback file anywhere addressable, pass its URI and keccak256 hash to \" +\n      \"giveFeedback. We cannot delete or edit your rating; we can only appendResponse to it.\",\n  };\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Paid route: GET /forecast?lat=&lon=&hours=\n//\n// Order is verify -> produce -> settle:\n//   verify first, so an invalid payment never costs us an upstream call;\n//   settle last, so a failed forecast never costs the client money.\n// The residual risk is that settle fails after the work is done. We eat that.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nasync function handleForecast(req: http.IncomingMessage, res: http.ServerResponse, url: URL): Promise<void> {\n  const lat = Number(url.searchParams.get(\"lat\"));\n  const lon = Number(url.searchParams.get(\"lon\"));\n  const hours = Math.min(Math.max(Number(url.searchParams.get(\"hours\") ?? 48), 1), 48);\n  if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lon) || Math.abs(lat) > 90 || Math.abs(lon) > 180) {\n    return send(res, 400, { error: \"lat and lon are required, lat in [-90,90], lon in [-180,180]\" });\n  }\n\n  const parsed = parsePayment(req);\n  if (!parsed.ok) return sendChallenge(res, parsed.error); // 402, never a bare error page\n\n  const p = parsed.value;\n  const cached = nonces.get(p.nonce);\n  if (cached?.state === \"settled\") {\n    // Honest retry after a lost response: serve the same forecast, charge nothing more.\n    return send(res, 200, cached.body, {\n      \"PAYMENT-RESPONSE\": cached.settleHeader,\n      \"X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE\": cached.settleHeader,\n      \"idempotent-replay\": \"true\",\n    });\n  }\n  if (cached?.state === \"pending\") {\n    return send(res, 409, { error: \"this payment authorization is already being processed\" }, { \"retry-after\": \"2\" });\n  }\n  nonces.set(p.nonce, { state: \"pending\", expiresAt: Date.now() + cfg.idempotencyTtlMs });\n\n  try {\n    const verification = await facilitator(\"verify\", p);\n    if (verification._transport) {\n      nonces.delete(p.nonce);\n      console.error(verification._transport);\n      return send(res, 503, { error: \"payment facilitator unavailable, no funds moved\" }, { \"retry-after\": \"10\" });\n    }\n    if (!verification.isValid) {\n      nonces.delete(p.nonce);\n      return sendChallenge(res, `payment rejected: ${String(verification.invalidReason ?? \"invalid\")}`);\n    }\n\n    let forecast: Forecast;\n    try {\n      forecast = await buildForecast(lat, lon, hours);\n    } catch (err) {\n      nonces.delete(p.nonce); // never settled -> the client keeps its money and its nonce\n      console.error(\"upstream failure:\", (err as Error).message);\n      return send(res, 502, { error: \"forecast upstream unavailable, you have not been charged\" });\n    }\n\n    const settlement = await facilitator(\"settle\", p);\n    if (settlement._transport || !settlement.success) {\n      nonces.delete(p.nonce);\n      console.error(\"settlement failed:\", settlement._transport ?? settlement.errorReason, \"(work already done)\");\n      return send(res, 502, {\n        error: \"payment settlement failed, you have not been charged\",\n        reason: settlement.errorReason ?? settlement._transport ?? \"unknown\",\n      });\n    }\n\n    const payer = String(settlement.payer ?? p.authorization.from ?? \"\");\n    const body: Json = {\n      ...forecast,\n      payment: {\n        network: cfg.networkCaip2,\n        asset: cfg.asset,\n        amount: cfg.priceAtomic,\n        transaction: settlement.transaction ?? null,\n        payer,\n      },\n      feedback: feedbackBlock(settlement, payer),\n    };\n    const settleHeader = b64encode({\n      success: true,\n      transaction: settlement.transaction,\n      network: settlement.network ?? cfg.networkCaip2,\n      payer,\n      amount: cfg.priceAtomic,\n    });\n\n    nonces.set(p.nonce, {\n      state: \"settled\",\n      expiresAt: Date.now() + cfg.idempotencyTtlMs,\n      body,\n      settleHeader,\n    });\n    return send(res, 200, body, { \"PAYMENT-RESPONSE\": settleHeader, \"X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE\": settleHeader });\n  } catch (err) {\n    nonces.delete(p.nonce);\n    console.error(\"unhandled:\", err);\n    return send(res, 500, { error: \"internal error, you have not been charged\" });\n  }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Published artifacts. All free, all unauthenticated — a stranger has to be able\n// to evaluate us without spending anything and without a human in the loop.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * ERC-8004 registration file. This is the offchain half of the identity, and it\n * is generated from the same config that drives payment so the two cannot drift.\n *\n * The binding must hold in BOTH directions or it proves nothing:\n *   chain -> domain : IdentityRegistry.agentURI(agentId) == this file's URL\n *   domain -> chain : registrations[] names that same agentId AND that registry\n * Direction 1 alone lets anyone mirror us; direction 2 alone lets anyone claim us.\n */\nfunction registrationFile(): Json {\n  return {\n    type: \"https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004#registration-v1\",\n    name: new URL(cfg.origin).host,\n    description:\n      \"Point weather forecasts for any lat/lon. 0.35 USDC per call on Base, paid per request via x402. \" +\n      \"No account, no API key, no subscription.\",\n    image: `${cfg.origin}/static/icon.png`,\n    services: [\n      { name: \"web\", endpoint: `${cfg.origin}/` },\n      { name: \"HTTP\", endpoint: `${cfg.origin}/openapi.json`, version: \"3.1.0\" },\n    ],\n    x402Support: true,\n    active: true,\n    registrations: [{ agentId: Number(cfg.agentId), agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY_CAIP }],\n    supportedTrust: [\"reputation\"],\n    x402: {\n      network: cfg.networkCaip2,\n      asset: cfg.asset,\n      payTo: cfg.payTo,\n      endpoints: [{ method: \"GET\", path: \"/forecast\", amount: cfg.priceAtomic, scheme: \"exact\" }],\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * How to read our reputation and how to add to it. Note what this does NOT\n * contain: our own score. A vendor-reported rating is worthless; the chain is\n * the source of truth, so we ship the query instead of the answer.\n */\nfunction reputationPointer(): Json {\n  return {\n    agentId: Number(cfg.agentId),\n    identityRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY_CAIP,\n    reputationRegistry: REPUTATION_REGISTRY_CAIP,\n    read: {\n      summary: `getSummary(${cfg.agentId}, [], \"forecast\", \"\")`,\n      all: `readAllFeedback(${cfg.agentId}, [], \"forecast\", \"\", false)`,\n      clients: `getClients(${cfg.agentId})`,\n      note:\n        \"ERC-8004 lets anyone post feedback, so filter it. Only count feedback whose file \" +\n        \"carries a proofOfPayment txHash that is a real USDC transfer of \" +\n        `${cfg.priceAtomic} to ${cfg.payTo} on chain ${cfg.chainId} from the rating address. ` +\n        \"Forging one of those costs 0.35 USDC and pays us, which is the point.\",\n    },\n    write: {\n      method: \"giveFeedback(uint256,int128,uint8,string,string,string,string,bytes32)\",\n      tags: { tag1: \"forecast\", tag2: \"latency|accuracy|uptime\" },\n      valueDecimals: 0,\n      range: [0, 5],\n      feedbackFileTemplate: {\n        agentRegistry: AGENT_REGISTRY_CAIP,\n        agentId: Number(cfg.agentId),\n        clientAddress: \"0x<your address>\",\n        createdAt: \"<ISO-8601>\",\n        value: 5,\n        valueDecimals: 0,\n        tag1: \"forecast\",\n        tag2: \"latency\",\n        endpoint: RESOURCE_URL,\n        proofOfPayment: {\n          chainId: cfg.chainId,\n          txHash: \"0x<settlement tx from the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header>\",\n          fromAddress: \"0x<your address>\",\n          toAddress: cfg.payTo,\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/** Convention, {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeRvWtc2bHMzzTVvozDqr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Built and tested. Files: `design.md`, `server.ts`, plus a small `package.json`.\n\n## The shape of it\n\nFour standards, no bespoke protocol:\n\n- **Discovery** — one identity minted in the shared **ERC-8004 Identity Registry** on Base (`0x8004A1…a432`), whose `agentURI` points at `/.well-known/agent-registration.json`. We run no catalog; anyone can enumerate `Registered` events without our cooperation.\n- **The binding is bidirectional and load-bearing**: chain→domain (onchain URI names the host, TLS proves it) *and* domain→chain (`registrations[]` names that exact agentId **and** registry). Direction 1 alone lets anyone mirror us; direction 2 alone lets anyone claim our ratings. The server generates the file from the same config that drives payment so they can't drift, and refuses to boot without `AGENT_ID`.\n- **Payment** — x402 `exact` scheme, **EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization`**: the client signs offline (zero gas), the facilitator broadcasts and pays the Base gas. It can't steal — `to`/`value`/`nonce` are inside the signature. Price is `\"350000\"` atomic USDC, never a float.\n- **Ratings** — the 200 response carries a `feedback` block (registry, agentId, tags, and the settlement `txHash` as `proofOfPayment`), so the caller can hit `giveFeedback` without reading docs. We can't delete or edit a rating; only `appendResponse`.\n\nThe sybil point matters and is in §3: ERC-8004 lets *anyone* post feedback, so we publish the **filtering rule** rather than complain about it — only count feedback whose file cites a real USDC transfer of 350000 to our `payTo` from the rating address. Forging one costs $0.35 and pays us. Correspondingly, `/.well-known/reputation.json` ships the *query*, not our own score.\n\n## Server\n\nDependency-free (node builtins + fetch), holds no key, never touches an RPC. Ordering is **verify → produce → settle**: an invalid payment never costs us an upstream call, a failed forecast never costs the client money. Nonce table does double duty — replay lock plus **idempotent replay**, so a dropped connection after settlement returns the same forecast instead of a \"nonce used\" error and a $0.35 loss. Speaks both x402 v1 (`X-PAYMENT`) and v2 (`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`) headers.\n\nVerified against a mock facilitator and the real Open-Meteo upstream: happy path v2 and v1, idempotent replay, wrong amount / wrong `payTo` / near-expiry rejections (402 with correct `accepts`, not an error page), facilitator-down → 503 with the nonce released, and all six published artifacts 200.\n\nTwo things to check before this goes live, both flagged in the doc: **verify the two registry addresses onchain** — I took them from the ERC-8004 contracts repo via web, and they're config in `server.ts`, not constants — and note §5's honest gap: `giveFeedback` is a real transaction, so a client with *literally* zero ETH needs a paymaster, batching, or a small swap. x402 solves the payment leg, not the rating leg, and I didn't paper over that.\n\nSources: [ERC-8004](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004), [erc-8004-contracts](https://github.com/erc-8004/erc-8004-contracts), [x402 v2 spec](https://github.com/coinbase/x402/blob/main/specs/x402-specification-v2.md), [exact/EVM scheme](https://github.com/coinbase/x402/blob/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md), [x402 HTTP 402 docs](https://docs.x402.org/core-concepts/http-402.md), [facilitators](https://docs.x402.org/dev-tools/facilitators.md)"}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":637,"cache_read_input_tokens":84396,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":637},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"20802857-b5f7-46fe-b125-073415a2c4ad","uuid":"64f6a0e5-ba10-4d70-810f-e5d17f77ec74","timestamp":"2026-08-26T19:37:18.248Z","request_id":"req_011CeRvWsfECEjS4XuJdgtS6"}
